description.en-US: File ops: read / list / grep / write (undoable via backup) / delete
description.zh-CN: 文件读写与检索：读 / 列目录 / 搜索 / 写（带备份可撤销）/ 删除

tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file from the local filesystem. Pass an absolute path. Returns {path, size, truncated, revision, content}; content is capped at max_bytes (default 32KiB) but `revision` always covers the FULL file. Read before edit_replace so old_string can be copied character-for-character, and pass the `revision` as `expected_revision` on any later fs_write / edit / fs_delete of this file — write tools reject stale observations.
tools.name: fs_read

path.description: absolute file path (required; must be inside the allowed workspace roots)

tools.description: List a directory. Pass an absolute path. Returns {path, entries: [{name, kind: file|dir|other, size}]}; directories come first, then names sorted.
tools.name: fs_list

path.description: absolute directory path (required; must be inside the allowed workspace roots)

tools.description: Case-insensitive substring search in a text file, or recursively under a directory. Pass an absolute path. Returns {query, matches: [{file, line, text}], truncated, scanned}. Use this instead of shell grep/findstr pipelines for content search — it is scoped to the workspace roots and returns structured matches.
tools.name: fs_grep

path.description: absolute file or directory path (required; must be inside the allowed workspace roots)

tools.description: Write a UTF-8 text file (create or overwrite). Args: path (absolute), content, create_dirs (bool, default false), expected_revision — the `revision` from a previous fs_read of this file; pass null ONLY to create a file that must not exist yet (the call is rejected if the file already exists without a revision, so blind overwrites are impossible). The previous content, if any, is backed up automatically; the result carries {path, bytes, existed, backup, revision} — pass that `revision` as `expected_revision` on your next write to this file, or pass the original output to fs_restore to undo.
tools.name: fs_write

expected_revision.description: revision from fs_read or the previous write's result; null = create a new file (rejected if the file exists)

path.description: absolute file path (required; must be inside the allowed workspace roots)

tools.description: Delete a file (directories are rejected in v1). Args: path (absolute), expected_revision (the `revision` from fs_read — deleting must prove the file hasn't changed since you observed it, so an externally modified file is never deleted blind). Irreversible — no backup is kept, the call requires user approval.
tools.name: fs_delete

expected_revision.description: revision from fs_read; the call is rejected if the file changed since you observed it

path.description: absolute file path (required; must be inside the allowed workspace roots)

tools.description: Undo a previous fs_write / edit_replace / edit_lines / edit_diff by restoring its automatic backup (the backup is consumed; restoring twice is a no-op). Either the compensation layer or you can invoke it: pass the original call's {call_id, args, output} from the transcript; only output.{path, backup, existed} is used. The result carries the restored file's `revision` — pass it as expected_revision on your next edit. Irreversible — restoring overwrites the file's current content, so the call requires user approval.
tools.name: fs_restore

call_id.description: id of the original fs_write call
